answer: In decentralized AI networks, Sybil resistance mechanisms like the kernel-based voting scheme can mitigate fake-identity attacks. This scheme works by requiring agents to prove their unique identity through a one-time, computationally expensive task, rendering it unfeasible for attackers to create multiple identities. As a result, the network resembles the tundra, where few agents can survive without genuine reputation. When an agent is honest, its vote is amplified, creating an echo effect that reinforces the legitimacy of its contributions, thereby securing the network against Sybil attacks.
